analysis.title: The Most Dangerous Part Of The Squeeze (The morning after the squeeze)
key_insights: SPX went from extreme oversold to major resistance in one session. The 7350-7400 area is big resistance with the 200-day moving average there, and the longer-term trend sits near 7200 (cash levels).
BTIG: 42 prior instances since 1985 of NDX rallying 6% or more while closing below its 200-day MA. Median 30-day return was -5.35% and the market was higher only 39% of the time.
NDX futures remain well below the 200-day MA with the short-term descending trendline intact, and even this rally did not reclaim the 21-day MA, showing how beaten up tech is.

BTIG: only twelve instances since 1985 of NDX falling 5%+ one day and rallying 5%+ the next. Only two saw positive returns the following day, average five-day return was -4.9%, and average max drawdown over the next 30 trading days was 16.4%.
Following those twelve reversals the average max draw-up over 30 trading days was almost 10%, but most of the biggest upside came after the first 15 trading days.

GS: S&P E-mini open interest rose $36.6bn between Nov 17 and 20 as the index fell 5.9%, with Friday alone +$26.6bn, the largest single-day change of 2026 outside roll periods. Monday's squeeze cut open interest by only $7.9bn, suggesting fresh longs, lingering bears, or both.
Bitcoin has given back much of the Jensen spike, opening a gap versus NDX that is flagged as a liquidity thermometer to watch.

JPM's Ron Adler says removing the Jensen uncertainty is positive for NVDA, but presidential intervention in corporate governance is a bigger risk that could weigh on multiples. He sees room for the rally to run given positioning but doubts a return to peak euphoria.

UBS: AI investor focus has shifted from spending scale to returns on spending. Expect more differentiation between companies funding AI internally and those reliant on debt, so the next phase is about dispersion more than beta.
UBS stays neutral on US and global equities and sees the rebound as a chance to cut megacap tech concentration, favoring equal-weight equities, European equities, industrials and health care.
VIX is near 30 after the prior day's vol spike despite SPX futures down less than 1%, close to March peak panic levels when SPX was about 700 points lower.
